title: Primary Function
learningObjectives: Connect crane function to pivot load transfer.
student: State the primary function of the shop crane and the structural role of the upper boom-to-mast pivot connection.
instructor: The crane lifts and positions heavy components. The upper pivot joins the boom to the mast assembly, transfers force, and permits boom rotation.

title: External Loads
learningObjectives: Distinguish hook load from local pivot force.
student: Identify the principal lifting load and explain why the local pivot force need not equal the suspended hook load.
instructor: The hook load enters the boom, but the pivot force depends on boom geometry, the hydraulic ram, reactions, and frame interaction. F is therefore supplied as an equivalent local teaching load.

title: Supports and Boundary Conditions
learningObjectives: Explain force transfer and rotation at the pin.
student: Identify the members joined at the upper pivot and describe how the pin permits rotation while transferring force.
instructor: The central boom lug lies between two outer mast-clevis plates. The pin passes through all three plates, transfers transverse force, and permits relative rotation.

title: Load Path
learningObjectives: Trace force through the selected joint.
student: Trace the qualitative load path from the hook and boom through the upper pivot toward the mast and base.
instructor: Hook demand enters the boom, reaches the central lug, crosses the pin into the two clevis plates, and continues through the mast/frame and base to the floor.

title: Critical Connection
student: Identify the exact connection and local components analyzed in this problem.
instructor: The selected connection is the large upper boom-to-mast pivot, comprising the pin, central boom lug, and two outer clevis plates. The lower ram pin is not analyzed.

title: Relevant Mechanical Responses
learningObjectives: Distinguish average pin shear and plate bearing.
student: Identify the assigned pin-shear and plate-bearing checks and distinguish them physically.
instructor: Pin shear acts across two transverse pin sections. Bearing represents compressive contact averaged over projected plate area td.

title: Relevant Parameters
student: Identify F, d, t_b, t_c, tau_allow, and sigma_b,allow and explain where each enters the model.
instructor: F sets demand; d controls pin area and bearing width; t_b and t_c set the corresponding projected areas; the two allowables define the teaching comparisons.

title: Student-Generated Structural Idealization
student: Draw a central boom lug between two outer clevis plates. Show the pin, two shear planes, full F on the central lug, and F/2 carried by each outer plate.
instructor: A complete model shows one central plate, two equal outer plates, a cylindrical pin, two shear planes, F on the central lug, and symmetric F/2 outer reactions.

title: Modeling Assumptions
student: State the assumptions used to reduce the real upper pivot to the connection model.
instructor: Use static equivalent loading, symmetric double shear, F/2 outer sharing, a cylindrical pin, uniform average shear and projected bearing stress, and assigned geometry/allowables. Neglect all excluded local, frame, dynamic, and certification effects.

title: Analysis Plan
student: Outline the calculation sequence from load split through stresses, allowable ratios, governing mode, sensitivities, and assessment.
instructor: Find F/2, pin one-plane and total areas, pin shear, central and outer projected areas/bearing stresses, all three ratios, the minimum governing ratio, sensitivities, and limitations.

title: Connection Load Distribution
student: Determine the force carried by the central lug and by each outer clevis plate.
instructor: The central lug carries F = {{crane_pin_F_kN}} kN; each outer plate carries F/2 = {{crane_pin_Fplate_kN}} kN.

title: Pin Shear Area
student: Calculate A_p = pi d^2/4 for one shear plane and the total double-shear area 2A_p.
instructor: A_p = {{crane_pin_Ap_mm2}} mm2; 2A_p = {{crane_pin_Ashear_mm2}} mm2.

title: Average Pin Shear Stress
student: Calculate tau_pin = F/(2A_p).
instructor: tau_pin = {{crane_pin_tau_MPa}} MPa.

title: Pin Shear Allowable Comparison
student: Compare tau_pin with tau_allow and calculate n_shear = tau_allow/tau_pin.
instructor: n_shear = {{crane_pin_n_shear}}.

title: Central-Lug Bearing Stress
student: Calculate projected area t_b d and average bearing stress F/(t_b d).
instructor: A_b,boom = {{crane_pin_Ab_boom_mm2}} mm2; sigma_b,boom = {{crane_pin_sigma_boom_MPa}} MPa.

title: Central-Lug Allowable Comparison
student: Compare central-lug bearing stress with sigma_b,allow and calculate its ratio.
instructor: n_b,boom = {{crane_pin_n_boom}}.

title: Outer-Clevis Bearing Stress
student: Using F/2 on each plate, calculate t_c d and average outer-clevis bearing stress.
instructor: A_b,clevis = {{crane_pin_Ab_clevis_mm2}} mm2; sigma_b,clevis = {{crane_pin_sigma_clevis_MPa}} MPa.

title: Outer-Clevis Allowable Comparison
student: Compare outer-clevis bearing stress with sigma_b,allow and calculate its ratio.
instructor: n_b,clevis = {{crane_pin_n_clevis}}.

title: Governing Included Mode
student: Compare all three modeled ratios and identify the governing included check.
instructor: {{crane_pin_governing_mode}} governs the included checks at {{crane_pin_governing_ratio}}.

title: Load Sensitivity
student: Increase F by 25%. Recalculate all three stresses and ratios and determine whether the governing mode changes.
instructor: At F = {{crane_pin_F25_kN}} kN: tau = {{crane_pin_tau_F25_MPa}} MPa, central bearing = {{crane_pin_sigma_boom_F25_MPa}} MPa, outer bearing = {{crane_pin_sigma_clevis_F25_MPa}} MPa; ratios are {{crane_pin_n_shear_F25}}, {{crane_pin_n_boom_F25}}, {{crane_pin_n_clevis_F25}}. Governing: {{crane_pin_governing_F25}}.

title: Pin-Diameter Sensitivity
learningObjectives: Contrast inverse-square and inverse diameter scaling.
student: Increase d by 25%. Quantify changes in pin shear and both bearing stresses and explain why shear decreases faster.
instructor: At d = {{crane_pin_d25_mm}} mm, tau = {{crane_pin_tau_d25_MPa}} MPa, central bearing = {{crane_pin_sigma_boom_d25_MPa}} MPa, and outer bearing = {{crane_pin_sigma_clevis_d25_MPa}} MPa. Ratios are {{crane_pin_n_shear_d25}}, {{crane_pin_n_boom_d25}}, {{crane_pin_n_clevis_d25}}. Shear scales with 1/d2; bearing scales with 1/d.

title: Plate-Thickness Sensitivity
student: Explain how increasing t_b or t_c affects the corresponding bearing stress and why neither changes idealized pin shear.
instructor: {{crane_pin_thickness_assessment}}

title: Model Limitations
student: Identify important effects omitted by the average-stress model, including pin bending, contact pressure, tear-out/net-section behavior, clearance/eccentricity, fatigue, and frame interaction.
instructor: The model excludes pin bending and deformation, nonuniform/Hertz contact, tear-out, net-section tension, edge effects, plate bending, clearance, eccentricity, preload/friction, hole ovalization, welds, fatigue, impact, wear, dynamics, and frame interaction.

title: Engineering Assessment and Recommendation
student: Report all baseline ratios, the governing included response, whether each assigned criterion is met, one mechanics-based improvement, and important limitations. Do not claim crane certification.
instructor: {{crane_pin_assessment}}
